purpose: Build a verified, date-ordered chronology of material property events, documents, registrations and legal state transitions without collapsing distinct dates or evidence types.
core_principle: EVENT DATE ≠ DOCUMENT DATE ≠ REGISTRATION DATE ≠ LEGAL EFFECT DATE
event_ordering_rules: Primary ordering follows the relevant event or legal-effect date for the requested chronology purpose.
Document and registration dates remain visible as separate fields.
Where legal effect depends on registration, registration timing is shown separately and linked to the legal rule.
If two events share a date, ordering requires evidence or remains explicitly unordered.
Unknown dates are not silently estimated.
A missing historical record is not evidence that no event occurred.
rules: A chronology is an evidence-organising structure, not proof by itself.
Each material event must retain its source and property/date match.
A document appearing in chronological order does not itself establish its legal effect.
Current state must not be projected backward merely because it is known today.
Historical law is selected according to the applicable date and transition rules.
Conflicting dates remain visible until resolved by authoritative evidence.
hard_stops: Never use registration date as event date without authority.
Never use document date as legal-effect date without authority.
Never fill historical gaps with assumptions.
Never hide a material chronology conflict.
Never treat a chronology as a substitute for official property evidence.
